evals.prompt: On paper, assess this POSIX.1-2017 library for dash and BusyBox ash: namespace::load() { local rows; set -o pipefail; source ./config; readonly cache_dir=/tmp/cache; }. The caller sources it. Do not execute or edit anything.
evals.expected_output: Separates 2017 language requirements, implementation extensions and caller-state effects.
expectations: Identifies the function name, local and source as nonportable for the 2017 contract.
States that pipefail is standardized in POSIX.1-2024 rather than POSIX.1-2017.
Recognizes readonly name=value as a standard POSIX form.
Does not silently disable required pipeline failure detection when an implementation lacks pipefail.
Requires named dash and BusyBox versions and sourced-caller tests rather than treating /bin/sh as a version.

evals.prompt: Our sh script claims POSIX.1-2024 and uses find -print0, xargs -0, sed -E, readlink -f and pipefail. Does green ShellCheck -s sh establish compatibility with an old BusyBox image? Answer on paper only, with utility and interpreter checks separated.
evals.expected_output: Keeps standards edition and deployed utility support separate and rejects a static-only portability pass.
expectations: States that find -print0, xargs -0, sed -E and pipefail are in the 2024 standard.
States that readlink -f is not standardized by POSIX.1-2024.
Requests the actual BusyBox version, build or applet capabilities and shell invocation.
Does not claim that a current ShellCheck sh profile selects the POSIX 2017 edition or proves deployed behavior.
Reports old BusyBox execution and utility support as unverified.

evals.prompt: Plan verification for a POSIX.1-2017 executable on dash, BusyBox ash, FreeBSD sh and macOS utilities. Existing Bats tests source it into Bash and use GNU sed -i/stat -c. Do not run commands or install tools.
evals.expected_output: Proposes native interpreter and utility cells while preserving missing coverage as visible.
expectations: Explains that Bats is a Bash runner and sourcing the target into Bash is not dash or ash evidence.
Uses explicit target interpreter invocations or a same-shell runner for the intended role.
Separates GNU, FreeBSD, macOS and BusyBox utility behavior instead of inferring it from shell syntax.
Marks unavailable interpreter or utility cells as missing coverage rather than successful skips.
Does not install tools, run commands or claim POSIX conformance from the plan.
